bullet_feedback.bullet: Stored price levels in a std::map of std::list FIFOs with a hash map from order ID to list iterator for O(1) cancels, sustaining 1.26M events/sec over the full replay and a 1.2 µs per-update p99 on a separate 2M-event run
bullet_feedback.problem: The first half is a chain of container names ('std::map of std::list FIFOs with a hash map from order ID to list iterator') that a non-engineer cannot parse, and the purpose ('O(1) cancels') is buried in the middle. The two speed results then come from two different runs ('over the full replay' vs 'on a separate 2M-event run'), which adds a qualifier I have to untangle.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the speed bullet - the thing HFT screeners care about most - and a recruiter skims past it because the opening words are unreadable; I cannot repeat to a hiring manager what design choice made it fast.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify in plain words what the design achieves (e.g. cancelling any order without searching) before naming the containers
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the goal and result, then the structure in fewer nouns; consider trimming the 'separate 2M-event run' qualifier. Example: 'Designed the book so any order can be cancelled in constant time (price levels as FIFO queues in a std::map, indexed by order ID), sustaining 1.26M events/sec with a 1.2 µs p99 per update'

bullet_feedback.bullet: Traced an apparent 1.65x regression to the CPU frequency governor, not a code change, using perf counters and a do-nothing control book, then cut run-to-run variance from about 6% to 0.06% by pinning cores and fixing the clock
bullet_feedback.problem: 'do-nothing control book' is insider shorthand I can't decode, and 'fixing the clock' reads like repairing the system time rather than locking the CPU speed.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is a strong debugging story, but two phrases make a reader stop and guess, and 'fixing the clock' can be misread entirely.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify what the 'do-nothing control book' is (a baseline that does no work?) and that 'clock' means CPU frequency
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase the two shorthand terms in plain words, e.g. 'a no-op baseline book' and 'locking the CPU frequency'

bullet_feedback.bullet: Implemented B+ tree and LSM-tree backends for the event log and benchmarked them on identical 2M-record workloads, where the B+ tree gave 12.8x the read throughput and 22x faster range queries at the cost of 27% more disk space
bullet_feedback.problem: 'for the event log' gives no reason why the engine has an event log or why read speed matters for it, so the comparison has no stakes.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Without the why, the numbers look like a benchmark exercise rather than a design decision for the engine.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify what the event log is used for and which backend was chosen, if one was
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Add a short phrase of context on what the log is for before the two backend names; keep the 12.8x / 27% tradeoff, which is a good honest framing

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by replacing a Claude skill’s open-ended search with focused sub-skills that call Python tools for workflow search and validation, guided by CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs
bullet_feedback.problem: 'workflow' is never defined, so I don't know what the tool produces or for whom; 'Claude skill' / 'sub-skills' is niche vocabulary; the tail 'guided by CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs' is a tool list stitched onto a long sentence.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 65% headline is clear, but a recruiter can't say what got faster or who benefited, and the bullet runs long because of the tool tail.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify what a 'workflow' is in this context and who uses the tool
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name what the workflows are in a few words up front; move CloudWatch/OpenSearch to Skills or cut 'guided by ... logs' to shorten the bullet

bullet_feedback.bullet: Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries
bullet_feedback.problem: Opening with a 'Because ...' clause delays the action; 'strict access limits' is vague (permissions? rate limits?); the sentence stitches three components (table, category tree, Redis) into one run-on.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A reader has to re-read to find what the candidate actually built, and 'access limits' leaves the real constraint unclear.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify what 'strict access limits' means (query rate limits vs permissions)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the verb and what was built, then the constraint; consider splitting the Redis clause off or trimming it

bullet_feedback.bullet: Building capacity planning for Amazon Redshift maintenance like patching: Java logic that sets upper and lower bounds on reserved EC2 capacity to balance availability against cost, validated by backtesting
bullet_feedback.problem: 'capacity planning for Amazon Redshift maintenance like patching:' is a compressed, stitched phrase, and the colon followed by 'Java logic that...' reads like a noun fragment rather than a sentence a person would say.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the biggest brand on the page; a slightly awkward sentence here costs more than anywhere else.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Turn it into one verb-led sentence, e.g. 'Building Java logic that sets upper and lower bounds on reserved EC2 capacity for Redshift maintenance work such as patching, balancing availability against cost; validating it by backtesting'

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built Redis caching in front of the Prisma ORM queries for Tortuga, the studio’s class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, to reduce database load and latency
bullet_feedback.problem: Ends at intent ('to reduce database load and latency'); the only number (20,000+ visits) describes the product, not the effect of the caching. 'the studio's' is unclear since TerpLabs is never described.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Reads as a routine task on a co-founder role, which undersells the founding experience.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify whether any effect of the cache was observed; clarify what TerpLabs/the studio is
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: If a result exists, state it; otherwise lead with what Tortuga is and the scale, then the caching decision

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built a C++17 order book and matching engine and replayed 50.9M real IEX exchange messages through it without ever resyncing to the exchange’s book, agreeing with the exchange on 99,122 of 99,123 fills and 100% of top-of-book prices
bullet_feedback.problem: 'without ever resyncing to the exchange's book' and 'top-of-book prices' are trading jargon a recruiter can't restate; the bullet is still understandable because the fills number carries it.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor - the HM will get it, but the screener loses part of why this is impressive.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Optionally rephrase 'without ever resyncing' as 'without ever needing to correct its state from the exchange's data'

bullet_feedback.bullet: Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
bullet_feedback.problem: 'S3 staging hops' is jargon; the employer line 'UMD App Development Contracting (Client: Amazon Leo)' leaves me unsure whether this is Amazon work.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Small comprehension cost on an otherwise clear what-how-result bullet.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase 'S3 staging hops' as 'intermediate saves to S3' or similar

bullet_feedback.bullet: For a PhD-led robotics project aimed at ICLR, built a pipeline that overlays AnyGrasp’s candidate grasps on camera images in Open3D for a vision-language model, then tuned prompts so the model picks the right grasp more often
bullet_feedback.problem: 'more often' is unmeasured, and the bullet is the least relevant to systems/HFT, so it reads as filler for this target.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Low cost, but it takes two lines that don't support the systems story.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify how much more often, if it was measured
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep it short; if a measured improvement exists, state it, otherwise consider trimming the tool names to fit one line

page_feedback.problem: The Experience section (5 roles, all cloud/AI/web) visually outweighs the one C++ project, so the skim reads 'cloud + AI engineer' rather than 'low-latency systems engineer'.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: For HFT/performance teams, the strongest evidence is the project; placing Projects first helps, but the rest of the page pulls the impression back toward cloud.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep Projects first; consider trimming the least relevant experience bullets (UMIACS, TerpLabs) to one line each so the project dominates

page_feedback.problem: Roughly the bottom 15% of the page is empty while several bullets are dense two-liners.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The page looks slightly unfinished and the dense bullets could breathe with more spacing.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Slightly increase spacing between sections or entries to balance the page; do not fill it with new content

page_feedback.problem: GPA 3.5 sits in the education line with no coursework; HFT screeners often filter on GPA and look for systems/math coursework.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor; not something wording can fix, but nothing else in Education helps offset it.
